Subject: Request: Network fencing + isolation narrative for Dedicated and Private deployments (SOC2/SIG)

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of Acme's SOC 2 scoping and SIG intake we need a short (one-page) security architecture narrative and a high-level diagram that describes how Redwood fences customer workloads in both Dedicated (Redwood-managed GPU pools) and Private (customer VPC / on-prem) modes. Key items the review team asked for:

- Per-deployment boundary descriptions (control plane vs data plane)
- How tenant separation is enforced (network, compute, storage)
- KMS / key boundary and who holds keys for Private mode
- Egress policy and exfil controls (what can reach the public internet)
- Any expected customer responsibilities (routing, peering, firewall rules)

We are working to a compliance deadline next Wednesday (2027-02-17). Can you send a short narrative + diagram and call out any artifacts we can attach to the SIG/CAIQ answers?

Subject: Re: Request: Network fencing + isolation narrative for Dedicated and Private deployments (SOC2/SIG)

Hi Sarah —

Appreciate the clear list. I've drafted a concise narrative and attached a high-level diagram that maps the control/data plane boundaries for both Dedicated and Private modes. Notes up front: this is a customer-facing narrative intended for SIG/CAIQ reviewers, not an internal runbook. If you need deeper technical artifacts (config snippets, iptables examples, or traffic matrices) we can add an appendix.

High-level summary (included in attached PDF):
- Control plane (Redwood-managed): API, scheduler, and model catalog live in our control plane; control-plane traffic is authenticated and TLS-encrypted back to the customer deployment.
- Data plane (customer workloads): For Dedicated, customer inference runs on tenant-isolated GPU pools in our VPCs with network policies and per-tenant namespaces. For Private, the data plane runs inside the customer's VPC (or on-prem) and uses customer-managed routing and KMS.
- Tenant fencing: enforced via network policy (Calico/Cilium) + enforced namespace isolation at the orchestration layer; per-tenant RBAC at the orchestration and storage layers; strict host-level kernel hardening and seccomp profiles for Dedicated.
- KMS/keys: For Hosted/Dedicated we use Redwood-managed KMS for transient keys and envelope encryption; for Private customers the recommended pattern is customer-managed KMS with a remote HSM or cloud KMS integration (we include config examples in appendix).
- Egress controls: By default Dedicated deployments egress through a controlled NAT with egress filtering and allowlists; Private deployments can be configured to block public egress entirely and route through customer egress appliances.

Attachments included: network-fencing-narrative-v1.pdf, high-level-diagram-v1.png.

Internal reviewers (Laura / Karthik / Vanessa) — can you scan the narrative for anything that needs stronger language for SOC/SIG (e.g., replace "recommended" with "required" where appropriate, call out encryption-at-rest details, add evidence pointers)? If helpful I can pair with one of you for a quick 30-minute run-through tomorrow AM.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Jonas — quick pass below. Overall this is good; a few clarifications the acquirer team will look for:

- Tenant fencing: explicitly call out per-customer VNI/VLAN (or overlay VXLAN ID) for Dedicated where available; mention microsegmentation using Calico global network policies.
- Storage separation: note that object storage buckets used for model artefacts are namespaced per-tenant + bucket policies and server-side encryption.
- KMS: change wording to emphasize that for Private we require customer-managed KMS or a signed contract clause; for Dedicated we retain envelope keys but can offer customer-supplied master keys for enterprise agreements.
- Egress: add the default firewall posture (deny-by-default) and list outbound allowlists we support (CRLs, telemetry endpoints).
- Evidence pointers: include links to the encryption key rotation logs, per-tenant bucket ACL screenshots, and a sample network policy YAML.

I've attached a short appendix with suggested language edits and a sample tenant fencing diagram (tenant-fence-appendix.md). Happy to push an updated PDF after a quick sync.

Laura Bennett
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
